messages:
jamie: quick handoff — night shift. TL;DR: io spike on embed-store (eu-west1), partial read failures for regen routes, rollback + temp mitigations applied. posting short checklist below.

oncall-bot: ALERT: embed-store io-saturation eu-west1 (P2) — increased error rate 12:03 UTC — incident created #INC-2026
sasha: saw the alerts. rolled back the canary (model-v2b) at 12:08. errors dropped to baseline for most tenants but small QPS customers still get intermittent 503s.
raj: what mitigations did you apply aside from rollback?
sasha: increased read replicas by +2 in eu-west1 (manual scale), enabled KV-cache bypass for regen-route for 30m, set per-request embed read timeout -> 20s. logs & short notes in the incident ticket. runbook ref: /runbooks/embed-io
lee: autoscaler didn't kick because avg CPU stayed low — queue latency spiked. I added a queue-length alert and a manual scale step. there's a PR to fix the autoscaler decision logic: #3421 (working on tests).
jamie: next shift checklist: monitor 503 rate and tail latency on embed-store, watch queue-length (>100 => scale), keep rollback in place if errors resurface. DO NOT re-run the canary until autoscaler PR merges and we validate shard distribution.
raj: can you paste the quick query to check tail latency?
sasha: run: `kubectl exec -it proxy -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep embed_store_tail_latency` or check grafana panel "EmbedStore / Tail Latency" (eu-west1).
lee: added dashboard alert -> posts to #eng-oncall if p95 > 450ms or errors > 1%. also instrumented a short log-sampling to capture stack traces for failing requests.
jamie: PR/asks for next shift: @lee finish PR #3421, @raj triage canary logs and add stacktraces to INC-2026, @sasha follow up with infra on potential shard hotspotting and eviction patterns. if stable by 03:00 UTC we can discuss a cautious canary re-run (5%).
sasha: leaving latest logs + snippets in the ticket and a short diff of the timeout changes. handoff complete :raised_hands:
oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026 updated — status: mitigated -> monitoring
